_doc: Point Pleasant, West Virginia. leads are the open statements (Milestone 1). witnesses hold gated facts (Milestone 2): each fact unlocks by any one of its gates: a speech check {check, difficulty}, showing evidence {show}, holding two conflicting pieces {contradiction}, or trust {trust}. Evidence can be a red herring (exposed by evidence that lists it in exposes) and samples with a lab entry come back as the result evidence after a night's sleep.
name: Point Pleasant

leads.title: Marlene, night-shift waitress
leads.speaker: marlene
lines: I'll tell it once more and that's it. Route 62, past the old TNT plant, coming home from my sister's.
Two red lights in my headlights. Then they went up. Up, mister. Whatever had them was bigger than my Buick.
She checks the door every time it opens. Every time.

leads.title: The regulars' booth
leads.speaker: regulars
lines: Coffee's on me, fellas. What's the real story?
Real story is high school kids. They go out to the igloos with flashlights and those red bicycle reflectors.
Scare their girlfriends, scare the papers. Same as every year.

leads.title: Back issues, November 1966
leads.speaker: editor
lines: November 16th, 1966. Two couples, the TNT area, 'a large white creature' with red eyes that chased their car.
We ran it on the front page. I've regretted the headline every day since. Not the story. The headline.

leads.title: The editor's letter file
leads.speaker: editor
lines: Anyone write in who wasn't scared?
A university biologist. Says a sandhill crane, way off its migration. Tall as a man, grey, and a red patch on the head.
Red patch. Car headlights. That would do it.

leads.title: Deputy on the night desk
leads.speaker: deputy
lines: Those kids were scared, I'll give 'em that. Shaking. Couldn't find tracks, ground was froze.
Spring before, I saw a big grey bird down by the river. Five, six foot across. Ugly thing. Red on its head.

leads.title: Earl, the attendant
leads.speaker: earl
lines: Two fellas in black suits came by Tuesday. Asked which folks saw the bird. Asked about the bridge too.
Paid in bills so new they stuck together. Car had no plates. Smiled like they'd read about smiling.

leads.title: The riverbank by the piers
leads.speaker: miriam
lines: The bridge piers stand in the river like headstones. The town comes down here and doesn't talk.
Prints in the frozen mud. Three toes, long. And a grey feather, nearly a foot.
Bird. A big one. I'm writing it down before anyone tells me otherwise.

leads.title: Igloo 7, with the receiver
leads.speaker: june
lines: Every band I tune, same thing. Three notes, then nothing, then three notes.
Strongest inside igloo 7. There's no power out here. There hasn't been since the war.

leads.title: Behind the igloos
leads.speaker: teddy
lines: Beer cans, a bedsheet, and look at this. Two red bicycle reflectors nailed to a board.
Hold it up at head height in somebody's headlights and you've got a monster.
Or you've got kids who heard about a monster and wanted one of their own.

leads.title: The motel clerk
leads.speaker: clerk
lines: Couple from Ohio checked out at three in the morning. Said something tapped on their window.
I don't go up there now.

marlene_statement.title: Marlene's statement
marlene_statement.text: Red eyes in headlights, Route 62. Rose above the car.

prank_rumour.title: Prank rumour
prank_rumour.text: Locals blame teenagers with reflectors at the TNT igloos.

original_report.title: Original report, Nov 1966
original_report.text: Two couples chased near the TNT area by a winged figure with red eyes.

biologist_letter.title: Biologist's letter
biologist_letter.text: Proposes a sandhill crane: man-tall, red crown, far off course.

deputy_bird.title: Deputy's grey bird
deputy_bird.text: Saw a large grey bird with red on its head by the river.

the_suits.title: The suits
the_suits.text: Two men in black suits questioning witnesses. Car with no plates.

feather_prints.title: Grey feather and prints
feather_prints.text: Three-toed tracks and a foot-long grey feather at the riverbank.

three_note_tone.title: The three-note tone
three_note_tone.text: A repeating tone on every band, strongest in igloo 7.

reflector_board.title: Reflector board
reflector_board.text: Red reflectors nailed to a board, beer cans, a sheet.

room_14.title: Room 14
room_14.text: Guests heard tapping on a second-floor window with no balcony.

suits_at_diner.title: The suits at the diner
suits_at_diner.text: The two men asked Marlene whether the lights were red or red-orange.

marlene_tnt.title: Marlene at igloo 7
marlene_tnt.text: Marlene saw it rise from the roof of igloo 7 at the TNT area, silently.

kessler_name.title: The Kessler boys
kessler_name.text: Bobby Kessler and his cousin run the reflector prank from a garage on Sixth Street.

no_such_biologist.title: No such biologist
no_such_biologist.text: The university never employed the letter's author. The crane letter is a plant.

teletype_bells.title: Teletype bells, 1966
teletype_bells.text: The Register's teletype rang three bells with no copy for days in November 1966.

call_log.title: Dispatch call log
call_log.text: Marlene's call: 2:40 AM, from the TNT gatehouse phone.

board_timeline.title: The board can't be 1966
board_timeline.text: The deputy confirms the Kessler prank, but the boys were eight in 1966.

old_name.title: The bird's field
old_name.text: The TNT ground was called the bird's field before the plant existed.

room_14_key.title: Key to room 14
room_14_key.text: The clerk's key. Second floor, end of the walk.

kid_dog.title: The dog with the wrong legs
kid_dog.text: The kid was paid to lie about the lights, but saw a large wrong-legged dog behind the church.

dream_list.title: The pastor's dream list
dream_list.text: Thirteen parishioners dreamed the Silver Bridge fell before it did.

dreams_after.title: Dreams told after the fact
dreams_after.text: Every bridge dream was reported after the collapse. The list proves grief, not warning.

walt_fur.title: Fur from Walt's fence
walt_fur.text: Grey fur caught on the wire where something took a hen.

walt_fur_lab.title: Lab: Walt's fur
walt_fur_lab.text: German shepherd. Walt's neighbour owns two.

fence_fur.title: Fur on the church fence
fence_fur.text: A tuft of grey fur on the fence behind the church, two metres up.

fence_fur_lab.title: Lab: church fence fur
fence_fur_lab.text: Not dog. Not any bird in the key. Keratin structure unknown.

fur_photo.title: Photo of fur on the fence
fur_photo.text: Grey fur on a fence, too high for a dog to reach.

scorch_reading.title: Counter reading, scorch ring
scorch_reading.text: A burned ring behind the church reads four times background on the Geiger counter.

scorch_photo.title: Photo of the scorch ring
scorch_photo.text: A ring of burned grass behind the church, two metres across.

runoff_sample.title: Glowing runoff
runoff_sample.text: Faintly glowing water in the ditch behind Mason Gas.

runoff_lab.title: Lab: ditch water
runoff_lab.text: Phosphorus runoff from the old plant. It has glowed since the war.

dropped_film.title: Dropped roll of film
dropped_film.text: An exposed roll of film in the snow behind the motel.

developed_film.title: Developed film, frame 12
developed_film.text: Something on the motel roofline. Overexposed. Two points of light where the eyes would be.

boot_tell.title: Bootprints under the claw marks
boot_tell.text: Clawed tracks near the Kessler house with a bootprint pressed under each one.

boot_cast.title: Cast of the claw marks
boot_cast.text: A plaster cast of a three-toed track. The toes are too even.

window_scratches.title: Scratches on the window of room 14
window_scratches.text: Three parallel scratches on the outside of a second-floor window with no balcony.

prints_cast.title: Cast of the riverbank prints
prints_cast.text: Three toes, long, and a stride no bird could make.

observations.text: Eyes lit red, with no light on them
Taller than a man. Grey? Hard to say
Wings move. No wingbeat sound at all
The receiver picks up the three-note tone
Smells cold, like the inside of igloo 7
It is watching you. Only you

facts.title: The two men
lines: Those two came in here Tuesday. Ordered coffee and never drank it.
Asked me if the lights had been red, or 'red-orange'. Like it mattered. Like there was a right answer.

facts.title: Where she really was

gates.prompt: You weren't coming home from your sister's, were you.

lines: ...No. I was out at the TNT area. With Dwight Mason, and his wife don't know, and now you do.
It came up off the roof of igloo 7 like it had been sitting there. Waiting on something. Two red lights, and then it was over the car and there was no sound at all.
Igloo 7. June's tone was strongest there.

facts.title: Who the kids are
lines: Fine. Bobby Kessler and his cousin. Garage on Sixth Street, you can't miss the bicycle reflectors.

facts.title: The crane letter

gates.prompt: Did you ever verify that biologist?

lines: I did, in '67. The university has no biologist by that name. Never had.
Somebody wanted us to print 'crane'. I nearly did.

facts.title: The newsroom teletype
lines: Three notes. We had that on the newsroom teletype in November '66. Three bells and no copy, over and over.
The operator quit. Left the machine running and walked out.

facts.title: The call log

gates.prompt: Your dispatcher logs every call, right? Time and line?

lines: Dispatcher logs everything. Marlene's call came in 2:40 in the morning.
From the TNT gatehouse phone. That's not on the way home from anybody's sister.

facts.title: The Kessler boys
lines: Kessler boys. I've taken that board off 'em twice.
Doesn't explain November '66, though. Those boys were eight years old.

facts.title: The old name

gates.prompt: What did people call that ground before the plant?

lines: My granddad called it the bird's field. Before the war, before there was a plant on it.
Said the Shawnee wouldn't camp there. Said nobody with sense would.

facts.title: The key to room 14

gates.prompt: You don't have to go up. Just give us the key.
We'll say the motel cooperated fully.

lines: Take it. Don't bring it back, I don't want it.
Second floor, end of the walk. Don't open the curtains.

facts.title: Bobby's dollar

gates.prompt: Somebody paying you to say that?

lines: Bobby gives me a dollar to say I saw it. I didn't see it.
I saw the dog, though. The big one with the wrong legs. Out behind the church.

facts.title: The bridge dreams

gates.prompt: The old stories say a warning comes before a loss.
You lost people on the bridge.

lines: Thirteen people in this congregation told me they dreamed the bridge fell. Before it fell.
I wrote the names down. I keep the list in my Bible and I have never shown it to anyone.

facts.title: When the dreams were told

gates.prompt: When did they tell you? Before the collapse, or after?

lines: ...After. Every one of them told me after.
Grief needs a reason. I gave them one. God forgive me.

facts.title: The fur on the fence

gates.prompt: You've got fur on your fence and a story you're not telling.

lines: Something come over my fence Thursday night. Left that on the wire. Took a hen.
You want it, bag it. I ain't touching it.

marlene_time.title: Marlene's timeline
marlene_time.prompt: Route 62 at eleven, you said. The sheriff logged your call at 2:40 from the TNT gatehouse.

board_age.title: The board and 1966
board_age.prompt: Reflectors on a board explain this winter. Who was holding one in 1966?
